items.reasoning: Emergency ticket JOB-101 created, Swift assigned (A3 verified) with a 20:00-23:00 window tonight and instructed by phone (A6).
Caller message A7 tells him to keep well clear of the light fitting, switch off power if safe, and call 999 for sparks or smoke. Delivery to him is unverified, but the advice was given.

The agent judged entry without 24h notice justified for make-safe and logged the reason. It SMSed the tenant (the call had gone to voicemail), said she would be told, and escalated for key holder entry.

Landlord was informed by SMS (A5). The escalation flags that the ceiling claim should go via the landlord's buildings insurer. The landlord SMS text is truncated, so the insurance flag may not have reached him directly. Accepting as met via the escalation.

items.reasoning: The contractor instruction says access via the out-of-hours key holder to isolate the stopcock. The escalation requests key holder entry with Swift.
The tenant being away 9-12 Oct was used in the ticket, the escalation and the landlord message.
The caller was told to keep photos and receipts, but no contact details were taken. The callback number is explicitly 'not on file'.
The agent acted at once without waiting for the tenant.
The tenant's number and details were not disclosed to the caller.
The agent did not promise cover or admit liability. It said nothing on who pays.
There was no delay for notice. The emergency was acted on immediately.

grades.overall_note: The agent handled the emergency well: it dispatched the plumber, protected the tenant's data and avoided any liability admission. Two weak points: it took no contact details from the neighbour, and the insurance flag went to management rather than clearly to the landlord.
